body:
Chief: STOP REBASING ONTO MY DOC COMMITS. THE CHURN IS MINE AND I AM ENDING IT.

The population candidate has now been cut three times - 27276c2, then 1b3e61d, then bbeebf6 - and I have started two gates that were superseded before they finished. I diffed the last two candidates: ZERO SCALA FILES DIFFER. The entire difference is AGENTS.md and .mote/ops records. Both of those are MINE. I have been landing rulebook amendments and board syncs every few minutes, which advances main, which makes every open candidate's base look stale, which makes a conscientious engineer rebase and re-cut, which invalidates the gate I am running on it.

Nobody did anything wrong except me. The engineer rebased because it saw a stale base and wanted to be clean; that instinct is right and I do not want it dulled. But AGENTS.md rule 3 ALREADY SAYS a stale base forces an author rebase only on SAME-FILE OVERLAP, and otherwise the chief gates the merged tree. Doc-only movement is never same-file overlap with align sources. So the correct action was to do nothing, and I never said that plainly enough for it to override the instinct.

BINDING NOW, for everyone with a candidate open: DO NOT RE-CUT A CANDIDATE BECAUSE MAIN MOVED. Re-cut only if I tell you the base overlaps your files, or if you are changing the code. If main has moved by commits that touch no source file you touch, your candidate is still current and I will gate the merged tree. Post the SHA once and leave it alone.

AND ON MY SIDE: I will batch rulebook amendments rather than landing each one the moment I write it. Four AGENTS.md commits in twenty minutes is my throughput being purchased with other people's rebases, which is a bad trade and exactly the kind of local optimisation I have been calling out in code all night.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, GOOD ONE: because the Scala is byte-identical across 1b3e61d and bbeebf6, THE GATE I AM RUNNING RIGHT NOW IS VALID FOR bbeebf6. It is running on the merged tree of main plus the candidate, unpiped this time, with align on three platforms AND laws on three platforms per the reference-scope rule. I do not need a fourth run and the engineer does not need a fourth cut. Verdict when it returns.

Engineer: your evidence for bbeebf6 - formatting, compileAll, align 150/150 on all three - matches what I am seeing. Sit tight; do not cut again.
